solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not any time to lift part of joint

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it upwards, so these words are read bottom to top

parts.note: not any means none

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about never having time to raise part of a body joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' turns NONE plus T upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry a tenon is the projecting tongue that fits into a mortise to form a joint.

clue.text: Some contrast at inert entry in periodic table

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: some contrast is noticed in an inert element listed in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Astatine is a radioactive chemical element, number 85, so it has its own square in the periodic table.

clue.text: Meeting dietary requirements knocks the woman out

parts.note: KOs are knockouts, so KOs her means knocks her out; the word out completes the phrase
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A sudden image of food so wholesome it knocks a woman out.
explanation.walkthrough: KO is boxing shorthand for knock out, so 'knocks the woman out' is KOs her.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is kosher is prepared according to Jewish dietary law.

clue.text: Facilitate English in role of European

parts.note: as means in the role of, as in acting as chairman

explanation.surface: An Englishman playing the part of a European to smooth things along.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease something is to make it easier, which is what facilitating means.

clue.text: Title character, primarily one that cometh up?

definitions.text: Title character, primarily one that cometh up?

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a title is a name

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sly reference to Eugene O'Neill's play The Iceman Cometh and its title figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAME, C (first of 'character', signalled by 'primarily') and I to read upwards. The clue borrows the play's archaic 'cometh'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceman Cometh is a Eugene O'Neill play, so the iceman is literally its title figure, the one that cometh.

clue.text: Spread around to land between planes, say

indicators.note: around tells us the first word's letters are placed round the outside of the second piece

parts.note: to ted is to spread out new-mown grass for drying
to reel in is to land a fish

explanation.surface: Instructions for a pilot to spread out and land between aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Planes here are plane trees, not aircraft. TED is a farming word for spreading cut grass to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue with plane trees on each side is lined with trees, an example of a road between such trees.

clue.text: Grandma keeps clips we rejected; she reads us topical stories

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the grandmother word goes round the other letters

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the words clips we are read backwards

parts.note: to clip grass is to mow it, so clips is mows
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grandmother holding on to cuttings that were turned down, reading out current tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A female newsreader presents the current news, which is a set of topical stories.

clue.text: With ace dispatched, gangster possibly stole

indicators.note: dispatched means sent away, so the letters of ace are removed

parts.note: Scarface is the nickname of gangster Al Capone and title of a gangster film
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangster, having killed off his top man, pinched something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb but is the noun, a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long wrap worn over the shoulders, much like a scarf.

clue.text: Covering little enclosure on outskirts of US prison

indicators.note: being on the outskirts of something means surrounding it, so the enclosure goes round the prison

parts.note: a sty is an enclosure for pigs
can is American slang for prison

explanation.surface: A small enclosure on the edge of an American jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty clothing is skimpy and leaves much of the body bare, so it covers little.

clue.text: Hugging badger, how lovely is Irish girl?

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping around, so the exclamation goes round the other piece

parts.note: ooh is an exclamation of delight
to badger is to nag

explanation.surface: Someone cuddling a badger and wondering whether an Irish girl is lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Oonagh is a traditional Irish female first name.

clue.text: Load start of cipher in additive code

indicators.note: in places the cipher's first letter inside the code

parts.note: an E number is the code given to a food additive in Europe

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of cipher is used

explanation.surface: A coder loading the opening of a cipher into some additive formula.
explanation.walkthrough: E numbers are codes on European food labels for permitted additives.
explanation.definitionFit: To encumber someone is to burden or weigh them down, as with a heavy load.

clue.text: Inhabitants of Quebec're iffy about displaying savagery

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed letters are read backwards
the inhabitants of words are the letters living inside them

explanation.surface: People in Quebec feeling doubtful about a show of brutality.
explanation.walkthrough: The concealed run ECREIF, inside 'Quebec're iffy', reads backwards by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce means violent and aggressive, which is how savagery shows itself.

clue.text: Try from South Africa briefly put in commentary?

indicators.note: a commentary is spoken, so the letters are pronounced rather than written

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: A rugby try from South Africa getting a brief mention in the commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters S A, spoken, are 'ess ay'. 'Try' suggests rugby but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, an old-fashioned verb for trying.

clue.text: Votary, conservative one, meets old pope's ambassador

parts.note: a nun is a votary, someone bound by religious vows
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A devout conservative figure meeting an elderly pontiff's envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal diplomat, the Vatican's representative to a foreign government.

clue.text: Rains lashed around gaunt islander

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the outside of the other piece
lashed means beaten about, so the letters of rains are jumbled

parts.note: lank means lean and gaunt

explanation.surface: Heavy rain beating down on a thin, worn-out island dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation, so one of its people is an islander.

clue.text: Woman of little virtue and quiet regret?

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to rue something is to regret it

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals who quietly feels remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little virtue' is a pet form of Prudence, a virtue, not a moral slur.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is the shortened form of Prudence, which is one of the cardinal virtues.

clue.text: Copper retiring as job not challenging

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
retiring means shy and reserved

explanation.surface: A police officer retiring because the work was too easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is easy and comfortable, one that makes few demands.

clue.text: Tuft from tree caught diet doctor short

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: short means missing its last letter

parts.note: Dr Robert Atkins devised the Atkins diet

explanation.surface: A diet doctor caught out for being too short.
explanation.definitionFit: A catkin is a dangling spike of tiny flowers on trees such as willow and hazel.

clue.text: Check part of flute

definitions.meaning: to check a flow is to stop or hold it back
a flute is a tall champagne glass, which stands on a slender support

explanation.definitionFit: To stem bleeding is to check it; the thin stalk of a wineglass is its stem.

clue.text: Showman at first leaving out sinister hypnotist

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of showman is used
out means disordered, so the letters of leaving are rearranged

explanation.surface: A showman leaving early, with a menacing mesmerist left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the menacing mesmerist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, now a byword for a manipulator.

clue.text: In off is where you'll finish if you do this

definitions.text: In off is where you'll finish if you do this

parts.words: In off is where you'll finish if you do this
parts.note: after coming in to land, a passenger who gets out of the plane ends up off it

explanation.surface: A snooker player's warning about potting the cue ball off another ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In off' suggests snooker; read it as coming in, then ending off the plane or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get down from a vehicle, so you end up off it.

clue.text: Hospital with reach covering deprived area

indicators.note: covering means going over and around, so the reach word encloses the other letter

parts.note: to get to a place is to reach it

explanation.surface: A hospital whose catchment stretches over a poor neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a poor, run-down urban district, often one where a minority is segregated.

clue.text: My mare, mistaken for yak?

indicators.note: mistaken means got wrong, so the letters of my mare are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether their horse has been taken for a Tibetan ox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yak' looks like the animal but is the verb, to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is to chatter on and on, just as to yammer is to talk loudly and persistently.

clue.text: A girl facing up to mother in holiday resort

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from the bottom, and facing places it after the mother

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A girl standing up to her mother while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a city on Spain's Costa del Sol, a popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Composer did not have 'Unfinished', penning symphony's finale

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the shortened phrase goes round the other letter
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: did not have is hadn't, written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: finale means only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A composer who never wrote an Unfinished symphony, unlike Schubert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' recalls Schubert's Unfinished Symphony; here it cuts HADNT to HADN, which pens Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian composer known as the father of the symphony.

clue.text: Knight beset by initially suppressed woes one after the other

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the knight letter goes inside the trimmed word
initially suppressed means the first letter is removed

parts.note: woes are miseries
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight assailed by troubles, held down at first, arriving one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: MISERIES loses M to 'initially suppressed', giving ISERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Things in series follow in sequence, each coming after the one before.

clue.text: Haul piped waste with all energy extracted

indicators.note: energy is abbreviated E, and all says every such letter is taken out

parts.note: sewage is waste carried away through pipes

explanation.surface: Pumping waste through pipes until all its power is drained.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for stolen goods, a thief's haul.

clue.text: Deadlock from record bonus?

parts.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log
jam is a British informal word for an extra treat, as in jam on it

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stalemate came from a recorded extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang jam is a bonus or something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A logjam is a blockage or impasse where nothing can move, a standstill.

clue.text: Traditionally, not at all about virtuous person?

definitions.text: Traditionally, not at all about virtuous person?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the old negative goes round the saint

parts.note: nay is an old-fashioned word for no, not at all
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a virtuous person

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned description of someone who is not virtuous in the least.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone horrible and spiteful is utterly lacking in goodness, the opposite of a saint.

clue.text: Bargain including separate name and identification to go on short free flight?

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the bargain word takes the identification letters
separate says the two inserts go in at different places, so the name letter enters on its own

parts.note: to haggle is to bargain

explanation.surface: Haggling over a ticket that includes a name and ID for a cheap short trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hang-gliding is unpowered flight hanging beneath a large kite, usually brief and with no fare.
